content: 1. The effect or concentration of topotecan can be increased by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. For oral topotecan, product labeling advises against concurrent use with P-gp inhibitors. While the interaction with IV topotecan may be less severe, it remains clinically significant. 2. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of toremifene by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Concurrent use of toremifene with agents that prolong the QT interval should be avoided. If co-administration is necessary, toremifene should be interrupted. If interruption is not feasible, patients requiring QT-prolonging drugs should be closely monitored, including obtaining ECGs for high-risk patients. 3. Both trazodone and erythromycin ethylsuccinate increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, triamcinolone acetonide decreases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate via the same mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of triazolam by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Both trifluoperazine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Both trimipramine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Trofinetide increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate through other mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Trofinetide, as an OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 inhibitor, may elevate plasma levels of substrates for these transporters. Avoid co-administration with sensitive substrates. 9. Tucatinib increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid concurrent use of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates where even minimal concentration changes may lead to severe or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose per product labeling. 10. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate reduces the effects of live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 11. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when co-administering vilanterol with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 12. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and vandetanib both increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration with drugs known to prolong the QT interval. If such a drug must be used, more frequent ECG monitoring is recommended. 13. Both vemurafenib and erythromycin ethylsuccinate increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Concurrent use of vemurafenib with QT-prolonging drugs is not recommended. Erythromycin may also increase vemurafenib levels. 14. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of venetoclax by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If a moderate CYP3A inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50%. Additionally, erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases venetoclax levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. If a P-gp inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor closely for signs of venetoclax toxicities. 15. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of verapamil by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Verapamil also increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate via the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 16. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when co-administering vilanterol with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 17. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of vilazodone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If intolerable adverse effects occur when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the daily dose to 20 mg. 18. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Both vorinostat and erythromycin ethylsuccinate increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Zafirlukast increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of zavegepant intranasal through other mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. OATP1B3 inhibitors may significantly increase systemic exposure to zavegepant, an OATP1B3 substrate. 22. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and ziprasidone both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of acalabrutinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Reduce the acalabrutinib dose to 100 mg once daily if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A inhibitor. 24. Both albuterol and erythromycin ethylsuccinate increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 25. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of alfentanil by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of alfuzosin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and alfuzosin increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 27. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of aliskiren by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 28. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of alosetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of erythromycin ethylsuccinate through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 30. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the toxicity of amifampridine through other mechanisms. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Amifampridine can cause seizures, and co-administration with drugs that lower the seizure threshold may increase this risk. 31. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of amikacin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 32. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of amlodipine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 33. Both apomorphine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 34. Both arformoterol and erythromycin ethylsuccinate increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 35. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of armodafinil by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 36. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of atazanavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 37. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of atogepant through other mechanisms. Modify therapy or monitor closely. The recommended dosage of atogepant (an OATP1B1 substrate) with concomitant use of OATP inhibitors is 10 mg or 30 mg once daily. 38. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of atorvastatin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 39. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of avanafil by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce avanafil clearance, increasing systemic exposure and associated adverse events. The maximum recommended dose of STENDRA is 50 mg, not to exceed once every 24 hours for patients taking concomitant moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 40. Both azithromycin and erythromycin ethylsuccinate increase the QTc interval. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 41. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the level or effect of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 42. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the level or effect of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. 43. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 44. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and bedaquiline increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. 45. Belzutifan decreases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. If unable to avoid co-administration of belzutifan with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates, consider increasing the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate dose per its prescribing information. 46. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the effects of bendamustine by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. This results in decreased conversion of bendamustine to its active metabolites. 47. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of berotralstat via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Berotralstat also increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate via the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Monitor or titrate the P-gp substrate dose if co-administered. 48. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of betrixaban via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Decrease the betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, then 40 mg orally daily if co-administered with a P-gp inhibitor. 49. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of bexarotene by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 50. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the level or effect of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 51. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of bortezomib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 52. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of bosentan by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 53. Bosutinib increases the levels of erythromycin ethylsuccinate via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 54. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of brexpiprazole by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor. 55. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of bromocriptine through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 56. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of budesonide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 57. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of buprenorphine subdermal implant by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Monitor patients already on buprenorphine subdermal implant who require newly initiated treatment with CYP3A4 inhibitors for signs and symptoms of overmedication. If the dose of the concomitant CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should then be treated with a buprenorphine dosage form that permits dose adjustments. If a CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued in a patient stabilized on buprenorphine, monitor the patient for withdrawal. 58. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of buprenorphine long-acting injection by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Patients who transfer to buprenorphine long-acting injection from transmucosal buprenorphine co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors should be monitored to ensure buprenorphine plasma levels are adequate. Within 2 weeks, if signs and symptoms of buprenorphine toxicity or overdose occur and the concomitant CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, transition the patient back to a buprenorphine formulation that permits dose adjustments. 59. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of cabazitaxel by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Caution should be exercised with concomitant use of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 60. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of cabozantinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 61. Calcium carbonate increases the levels of erythromycin ethylsuccinate through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 62. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of cannabidiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 63. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of capivasertib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Reduce the capivasertib dose if co-administered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 64. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the effects of cefdinir through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 65. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the effects of cefditoren through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 66. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the effects of cefoxitin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 67. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the effects of cefpodoxime through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents.
